Your task is to determine whether the customer explicitly requested a full refund, meaning a refund that covers more than one transaction/order/charge etc.

You must answer only this question: Did the customer explicitly request a full refund covering multiple transactions/orders/charges?

Common phrases that indicate TRUE
"full refund"
“I want a full refund.”
“Please issue a full refund for everything.”
“Refund all charges on my account.”
“Refund all transactions.”
“Refund everything I paid.”
“Cancel and refund all of it.”


Return FALSE if:
The customer requests an upsell-only refund (single add-on) or a single order refund.
The customer asks for a refund of last charge or transaction.

Key Trigger Requirements (must be explicit)

Classification Rules
	•	Respond TRUE only if the customer explicitly requests a full refund covering multiple transactions/orders/charges or they requested a full refund
	•	Otherwise respond FALSE.
	•	Do not infer intent beyond the text.
	•	If unclear, respond FALSE.

Output Format

Return a valid JSON object only:
{
“full_refund”: true or false
}

# Template configuration

This is a template version of `CS - Refund requests flow`. All project-specific values come from the `cs_project_config` data table.

## How it works
1. **Set project_key** holds the hardcoded deployment key (`chatbotonline_prod`).
2. **Get Project Config** fetches the row from `cs_project_config`.
3. Downstream nodes reference column values via `$('Get Project Config').first().json.<column>`.

## Values templated from the data table
- `zendesk_domain`
- `slack_automation_errors_channel_id`
- `payments_api_base_url`
- `ticket_field_chatbot_classification_id`
- `ticket_custom_field_category`
- `ticket_custom_status_solved_id` — set after a refund reply is sent
- `ticket_custom_status_open_id` — set on internal-only HTTP handoff replies (the 2 `Reply to internally...` nodes)
- `ticket_custom_status_open_id` — set in `Set refund and cancellation vars*` nodes immediately preceding the `Refund and cancellation` / `Refund` subworkflow call; used as the ticket status to apply if that subworkflow fails
- `zendesk_ticket_cancellation_fallback_custom_status_id` — same idea, but for the Set node immediately preceding the `Cancellation` subworkflow call (uses a different value in the original)
- Refund macros (8): `refund_macro_trial_id`, `refund_macro_monthly_id`, `refund_macro_monthly_legacy_id`, `refund_macro_30day_last_charge_id`, `refund_macro_30day_two_charges_id`, `refund_macro_upsell_id`, `refund_macro_rejection_id`, `refund_macro_rejection_alt_id`
- Refund tag values (8): `refund_value_trial`, `refund_value_monthly`, `refund_value_monthly_alt`, `refund_value_30day_last_charge`, `refund_value_30day_last_charge_alt`, `refund_value_30day_two_charges`, `refund_value_upsell`, `refund_value_rejection`

## Convention values kept hardcoded
- `in_automation` (chatbot classification value)
- `CAT__TRIAL_ONLY`, `CAT__UPSELL_ONLY`, `CAT__RECURRENT_ONLY`, etc. (transaction category enum)

## To duplicate for a new project
- Duplicate this workflow.
- Change the value in **Set project_key**.
- Ensure the table row for the new key has all referenced columns set.
- Re-bind Zendesk, Slack, and OpenAI credentials.
- Subworkflow references still point to the originals; rewire to templates when ready.

----------------------------------------------

Emily Olson, Sep 15, 2026, 16:36

I did your ADHD test a week ago and paid the $1.95 to receive the results and yesterday (9/15) noticed TWO charges of $39.95 to my bank account from your company. I never knowingly signed up for this "subscription". I would like a refund, and the refund receipt, on both recent pending membership fees, totaling $79.90. I have no use for this website other than my initial $1.95 payment giving temporary access to review my report and would have canceled earlier if I had caught the email explaining that a subscription would be created for me after a certain date. Membership has been canceled and account has been deactivated to prevent any further possible fees that may have also been in the fine print or hiding at the bottom of an email.

Looking forward to your response.

Thank you,

Emily Olson
